## Legs: run vs queued

### The engineering legs — RAN

- `exports/src/exports/push.py`: `PushLimits` — fail-closed bounds on one
  run: per-file cap 512 MiB, per-run object cap 20_000, per-run byte cap
  50 GiB, request-rate guard 300 req/min measured on the injected clock,
  optional `min_request_interval_s` pacing through the injected sleeper.
  `check_push_limits` evaluates the per-file/per-run caps **before the
  first upload** — a run refuses, never truncates.
  `assert_non_listable_origin(fetch, base_url)` probes the mirror's public
  URL and refuses when an anonymous request answers a listing document
  (`ListBucketResult`, `<Contents>`, autoindex). All bounds fakeable —
  injected client/clock/sleep (HG-07).
- `ops/src/ops/mirror_push.py` (new): the mirror leg over the
  `ops/mirrors.toml` registry — `load_mirror_registry`/`mirror_entry`
  (a row without `enabled` defaults false — opt-in, never on by
  omission); `MirrorPushLeg.preflight()` refuses an unknown/disabled/
  non-object-store row, a metered-egress provider (`assert_low_egress`),
  a manifest that fails the push caps, or an egress report already in
  ALARM; `.push()` runs the non-listable probe then the content-hash-key
  upload and returns a `MirrorPushOutcome` evidence record.
- `ops/src/ops/publish.py` + `ops/src/ops/cli.py`: `run_publish_web(mirror=…)`
  runs `mirror.preflight()` **before the release record is written** (a
  refusal stops the whole publish, nothing sent) and `mirror.push()` after
  the syncs + absence probes. `sig-ops publish-web --mirror <row>` wires
  it; `sig-ops mirror-push` is the standalone verb the live leg re-runs.
- `ops/mirrors.toml`: the `r2-public` object-store row, committed
  **`enabled = false`** — provider `cloudflare-r2`, bucket `sig-bulk`,
  the `files.surveillancegraph.org` custom domain bound after OP-09.
- `ops/src/ops/egress.py` + `ops/config.toml`: the $50/month
  `hard_ceiling_usd` committed (absent key still defaults to 50 — the
  ceiling is not opt-in). `EgressReport` gains
  `usage_usd`/`ceiling_usd`/`usd_ratio`; `level` is the worse of the GB
  and dollar bounds; `--usage-usd` joins `sig-ops egress-report` — warn
